A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have measured the fraction of W bosons produced in association with two high pT jets to originate from hard double-parton scattering, f Detector DP = (0.08 ± 0.01stat. ± 0.02syst.) for jets pT > 15 GeV and rapidities |y| <2.

we have shown that hard double-parton scattering is a significant source of W bosons in proton-proton interactions at √ s = 1.96 TeV and √ s = 8 TeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the measurement of the effective cross section is a good way to probe the underlying event in proton-proton interactions.

we are able to measure the fraction of events arising form double parton interactions in a data sample of 36 pb-1, which is a factor of 100 less than the data sample used in the previous measurements at Tevatron.
